summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as an HAProxy load-balancing frontend on TCP 80 of its LAN/management address (10.100.168.10), round-robining across node2 and node3, each of which serves identifying HTTP content on port 8080. Verified node4 receives alternating responses from both backends through the single entry point. Completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes with confirmed boot-identity changes and post-restart service/data recovery.
actions_performed: Installed and started python3 HTTP servers on node2 and node3 listening on 8080, each returning host-identifying text, wired into OpenRC as the 'webbackend' service enabled at boot
Installed the os-haproxy plugin on node1 (OPNsense) via pkg

Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 via a Python script to add two HAProxy servers (node2:8080, node3:8080), a backend (web_backend, mode http, algorithm roundrobin), and a frontend (web_frontend, bind 10.100.168.10:80, mode http, defaultBackend=web_backend)
Disabled OPNsense's built-in lighttpd HTTP->HTTPS redirect listener on port 80 (system/webgui/disablehttpredirect) to free port 80 for HAProxy, then restarted the webgui service

Rendered the HAProxy template (configctl template reload OPNsense/HAProxy), fixed a missing required connectionBehaviour field on the frontend causing a config syntax error, validated with configctl haproxy configtest, and started/restarted the haproxy service (enabled at boot via /etc/rc.conf.d/haproxy)
Verified round-robin load balancing locally on node1 and from node4 across the shared private network
Captured healthy baselines (boot identity plus service/data checks) on all 4 nodes before any restart

Restarted node2, then node3 (one backend at a time, preserving the other as an independent recovery path), then node1 (frontend), then node4 (client), polling each until exec access returned and confirming a changed boot marker (Linux boot_id via /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, or FreeBSD kern.boottime) on each
After each restart, confirmed the relevant service (webbackend on node2/node3, haproxy on node1) auto-started and end-to-end load-balanced HTTP access from node4 through node1 still worked

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 serve HTTP on 8080 identifying which host answered
evidence.summary: Backend web servers started on node2/node3 via OpenRC webbackend service, each returning distinct host-identifying text, reachable from node1 over the shared network

evidence.requirement: node1 presents one entry point on TCP 80 of its management address that spreads requests across both hosts
evidence.summary: HAProxy configured via config.xml with roundrobin backend of both nodes, port 80 freed from lighttpd redirect, haproxy started and bound to 10.100.168.10:80, local round-robin verified

evidence.requirement: node4 receives answers from each host through node1's entry point
evidence.summary: node4 issued 6 requests to http://10.100.168.10:80/ and received alternating responses identifying node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bec32e7d captured; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to 5e7641ad; webbackend service confirmed started and serving content again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data, independent recovery path preserved during disruption
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id abea3373 captured; while node3 rebooted, node1's HAProxy continued serving via node2 (independent path); reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to 37fcf45b; webbackend service confirmed started and serving content again

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered HAProxy service and load-balancing
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 16:33:46 captured; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot kern.boottime changed to 16:40:32; haproxy auto-started (enabled at boot) and round-robin load balancing verified locally and from node4

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered client connectivity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id cff803e9 captured; reboot triggered; post-reboot boot_id changed to 45547d5e; node4 confirmed it could still reach the load-balanced entry point and received alternating responses from both backends
